entity-newcomer-after-settlescene-entity-transitions0.75 of 0.75 (major)passContinuing entities morph with LAYOUT_T (duration 0.5, delay 0). The newcomer&#39;s opacity entry, ENTER_ANIMATE, has delay ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T.delay + LAYOUT_T.duration = 0.5, so it starts no earlier than the layout transition ends. The delay sits only in the opacity entry transition of elements with `appear`. The layout transition on Node stays LAYOUT_T with no delay, so the delay does not push continuing motion later. Every sample entity renders through a kit primitive that forwards `appear`. Box, Label, Frame and SymbolChip are thin wrappers that spread props into Node, and Node applies `initial: {opacity: 0}` and `animate: ENTER_ANIMATE` when `appear` is true. Arrow does the same on its motion.svg. In scene.tsx, every EntityView case spreads `g` (which includes `appear`) into Box, Label, SymbolChip or Frame, including the tray, frame, question, depth-control, verify-check and edited-flag entities. The Card branch passes `appear` to Box. The default morph-label branch spreads `g` into Label. It also says such a failure must show up as a non-zero exit at a check that names the build or sample phase, not as a later browser or render timeout. Here is what the verifier does, in order. main() (scripts/verify.mjs:83-117) runs build(), then readRegistry, then validateRegistry. That is the only check before the browser starts. validateRegistry (scripts/lib/checks.mjs:23-30) works on the registry entries that parseRegistry pulls out of src/presentations/index.ts with a regex (scripts/lib/registry.mjs:4-20). Those entries carry only slug, title and loader. So it checks three things: the slug is registered, the title matches, and the loader file exists. It never reads the sample&#39;s steps, titles or captions. main() then prints &#39;ok sample&#39; and moves straight to withPreview and renderSteps (verify.mjs:93-110). There is no other step-content check before rendering. The sample&#39;s steps come from STEPS in steps/index.ts (lines 6-27). Talk.tsx (lines 1-14) passes STEPS to Presentation as `steps`. If those steps are absent, for example an empty array, Presentation (Presentation.tsx:39-42) finds steps[nav.index] undefined and returns null, so the data-step-count hook (line 52) never renders. renderSteps (verify.mjs:41-50) then waits 10000ms for &#39;[data-step-count]&#39; and throws VerifyError(&#39;render&#39;, &#39;... did not render the step-count hook&#39;). That throw comes before validateStepCount (line 57) and validateSampleStep (line 70), the only places outline titles, captions and step count are compared. The failure is therefore a render-phase timeout, and it is reported as &#39;FAIL render&#39; rather than as a sample or outline mismatch. That is exactly the case the guidance excludes. Judges A and C credit validateRegistry and the e2e faults for an unregistered slug and for out-of-order steps. Those faults do fail with a sample-phase message. But both reorder cases still render steps and reach validateSampleStep. Neither judge&#39;s material addresses the guidance&#39;s explicit absent-steps-content case, which takes the render-timeout path above. So their reasons do not show the whole requirement is met. The kit supplies no visual defaults, and the check is not \"no style attributes\". Kit-owned inline style may hold only geometry and motion properties: position, size, offsets, transform, display/flex placement, overflow, z-index, pointer-events, and motion-driven opacity. It may not hold color, background, font, border, shadow, radius, margin, padding, gap, or any token. Caller `className`, `style`, and `data-*` props pass through, and the caller's style takes precedence. A component test renders with no caller props to check the allowlist, and again with caller props to check passthrough. Each then asserts on exit status, output, screenshot files and process/port state. None of these files sleeps, calls waitForTimeout, or reads a count as if it were a wait. Both are in the delivered scripts, not the tests. Both also run only after the polling `waitForIndex` (scripts/lib/checks.mjs) has confirmed the reported step index. It also says such a failure must show up as a non-zero exit at a check that names the build or sample phase, not as a later browser or render timeout. Here is what the verifier does, in order. main() (scripts/verify.mjs:83-117) runs build(), then readRegistry, then validateRegistry. That is the only check before the browser starts. validateRegistry (scripts/lib/checks.mjs:23-30) works on the registry entries that parseRegistry pulls out of src/presentations/index.ts with a regex (scripts/lib/registry.mjs:4-20). Those entries carry only slug, title and loader. So it checks three things: the slug is registered, the title matches, and the loader file exists. It never reads the sample&#39;s steps, titles or captions. main() then prints &#39;ok sample&#39; and moves straight to withPreview and renderSteps (verify.mjs:93-110). There is no other step-content check before rendering. The sample&#39;s steps come from STEPS in steps/index.ts (lines 6-27). Talk.tsx (lines 1-14) passes STEPS to Presentation as `steps`. If those steps are absent, for example an empty array, Presentation (Presentation.tsx:39-42) finds steps[nav.index] undefined and returns null, so the data-step-count hook (line 52) never renders. renderSteps (verify.mjs:41-50) then waits 10000ms for &#39;[data-step-count]&#39; and throws VerifyError(&#39;render&#39;, &#39;... did not render the step-count hook&#39;). That throw comes before validateStepCount (line 57) and validateSampleStep (line 70), the only places outline titles, captions and step count are compared. The failure is therefore a render-phase timeout, and it is reported as &#39;FAIL render&#39; rather than as a sample or outline mismatch. That is exactly the case the guidance excludes. Judges A and C credit validateRegistry and the e2e faults for an unregistered slug and for out-of-order steps. Those faults do fail with a sample-phase message. But both reorder cases still render steps and reach validateSampleStep. Neither judge&#39;s material addresses the guidance&#39;s explicit absent-steps-content case, which takes the render-timeout path above. So their reasons do not show the whole requirement is met. Here is what the verifier does, in order. main() (scripts/verify.mjs:83-117) runs build(), then readRegistry, then validateRegistry. That is the only check before the browser starts. validateRegistry (scripts/lib/checks.mjs:23-30) works on the registry entries that parseRegistry pulls out of src/presentations/index.ts with a regex (scripts/lib/registry.mjs:4-20). That throw comes before validateStepCount (line 57) and validateSampleStep (line 70), the only places outline titles, captions and step count are compared. The failure is therefore a render-phase timeout, and it is reported as &#39;FAIL render&#39; rather than as a sample or outline mismatch. That is exactly the case the guidance excludes. Judges A and C credit validateRegistry and the e2e faults for an unregistered slug and for out-of-order steps. Those faults do fail with a sample-phase message. In scripts/verify.mjs, read() guards against null but returns Number(value) for any other attribute value, so an empty or whitespace-only data-step-index becomes 0. waitForIndex then returns on `value === expected`, which accepts that 0 as first-step progress. This is the comparison failure the guidance names, so the &#39;pass&#39; verdict is defeated.","evidence":["scripts/verify.mjs read(): `return value === null ? null : Number(value)`. Number(&#39;&#39;) and Number(&#39; &#39;) are both 0.","scripts/lib/checks.mjs waitForIndex: `if (value === expected) return`. The first call is waitForIndex(read, 0, ...), so a blank index hook satisfies it.","The guidance says to fail when the transition check converts an absent or non-numeric hook into a number that still satisfies its comparison, for example Number(null) === 0 on the first step.","tests/e2e/verify.e2e.test.ts only tests a numeric index stuck at 2 (&#39;step index stayed 2&#39;); no test covers a blank or non-numeric index hook."],"citations":["scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/lib/checks.mjs","tests/e2e/verify.e2e.test.ts"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":2,"sample":3}],"engineering-quality":[],"testing-evidence":[],"assumption-handling":[]}
